requirements.original: ( ObjectReference | ( all port ) ) "." clear
requirements.canonical: The clear port operation has the syntax ( ObjectReference | all port ) "." clear.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.1 -- ( ObjectReference | ( all port ) ) "." clear

requirements.original: The clear operation removes the contents of the incoming queue of the specified port or of all ports of the test component performing the clear operation.
requirements.canonical: The `clear` operation removes the contents of the incoming queue of the specified port.
requirements.condition: an ObjectReference is specified

examples.text: myPort.clear; // clears port MyPort

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.1 -- The clear operation removes the contents of the incoming queue of the specified port or of all ports of the test component performing the clear operation.

requirements.original: The clear operation removes the contents of the incoming queue of the specified port or of all ports of the test component performing the clear operation.
requirements.canonical: When used with `all port`, the `clear` operation removes the contents of the incoming queues of all ports of the test component performing the clear operation.
requirements.condition: `all port` is used
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.1 -- The clear operation removes the contents of the incoming queue of the specified port or of all ports of the test component performing the clear operation.

requirements.original: If a port queue is already empty then this operation shall have no action on that port.
requirements.canonical: If a port queue is already empty, the `clear` operation SHALL have no action on that port.
requirements.condition: the port queue is already empty
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.1 -- If a port queue is already empty then this operation shall have no action on that port.

requirements.original: Table 25: Overview of TTCN-3 port operations: Clear port; Col2: clear
requirements.canonical: The clear port port operation IS denoted by the keyword `clear`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.1 -- Table 25: Overview of TTCN-3 port operations: Clear port; Col2: clear

requirements.original: Table 25: Overview of TTCN-3 port operations: Start port; Col2: start
requirements.canonical: The start port port operation IS denoted by the keyword `start`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.1 -- Table 25: Overview of TTCN-3 port operations: Start port; Col2: start

requirements.original: Table 25: Overview of TTCN-3 port operations: Stop port; Col2: stop
requirements.canonical: The stop port port operation IS denoted by the keyword `stop`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.1 -- Table 25: Overview of TTCN-3 port operations: Stop port; Col2: stop

requirements.original: Table 25: Overview of TTCN-3 port operations: Halt port; Col2: halt
requirements.canonical: The halt port port operation IS denoted by the keyword `halt`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.1 -- Table 25: Overview of TTCN-3 port operations: Halt port; Col2: halt

requirements.original: Table 25: Overview of TTCN-3 port operations: Check the state of a port; Col2: checkstate
requirements.canonical: The check the state of a port port operation IS denoted by the keyword `checkstate`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.1 -- Table 25: Overview of TTCN-3 port operations: Check the state of a port; Col2: checkstate

requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `clear` port operation SHALL be of a port type.

examples.text: myPort.clear; // clears port MyPort

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.1 -- a) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.

requirements.original: The start operation enables sending and receiving operations on the port(s).
requirements.canonical: The `start` port operation enables sending and receiving operations on the port or ports it is applied to.

examples.text: myPort.start; // starts myPort

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.2 -- The start operation enables sending and receiving operations on the port(s).

requirements.original: ( ObjectReference | ( all port ) ) "." start
requirements.canonical: The start port operation has the syntax ( ObjectReference | all port ) "." start.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.2 -- ( ObjectReference | ( all port ) ) "." start

requirements.original: If a port is defined as allowing receiving operations such as receive, getcall, etc. the start operation clears the incoming queue of the named port and starts listening for traffic over the port.
requirements.canonical: If a port allows receiving operations, the `start` operation clears the incoming queue of the named port.
requirements.condition: the port is defined as allowing receiving operations
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.2 -- If a port is defined as allowing receiving operations such as receive, getcall, etc. the start operation clears the incoming queue of the named port and starts listening for traffic over the port.

requirements.original: If a port is defined as allowing receiving operations such as receive, getcall, etc. the start operation clears the incoming queue of the named port and starts listening for traffic over the port.
requirements.canonical: If a port allows receiving operations, the `start` operation starts listening for traffic over the port.
requirements.condition: the port is defined as allowing receiving operations
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.2 -- If a port is defined as allowing receiving operations such as receive, getcall, etc. the start operation clears the incoming queue of the named port and starts listening for traffic over the port.

requirements.original: If the port is defined to allow sending operations then the operations such as send, call, raise, etc. are also allowed to be performed at that port.
requirements.canonical: If a port allows sending operations, after the `start` operation sending operations such as `send`, `call` and `raise` MAY be performed at that port.
requirements.condition: the port is defined to allow sending operations and has been started
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.2 -- If the port is defined to allow sending operations then the operations such as send, call, raise, etc. are also allowed to be performed at that port.

requirements.original: By default, all ports of a component shall be started implicitly when a component is created.
requirements.canonical: All ports of a test component SHALL be started implicitly when the component is created.
requirements.condition: by default
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.2 -- By default, all ports of a component shall be started implicitly when a component is created.

requirements.original: The start port operation will cause unstopped ports to be restarted by removing all messages waiting in the incoming queue.
requirements.canonical: A `start` operation applied to an unstopped port restarts the port by removing all messages waiting in the incoming queue.
requirements.condition: the port is not stopped

readings: A `start` operation applied to an already started port restarts it by removing all messages waiting in the incoming queue.
A `start` operation applied to a port that is not in the stopped state (started or halted) clears its incoming queue.
ambiguity.issue: 'unstopped ports' is not a defined port state; chose the reading that covers every non-stopped port (started or halted), consistent with NOTE 3 of 22.5.4.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.2 -- The start port operation will cause unstopped ports to be restarted by removing all messages waiting in the incoming queue.

requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `start` port operation SHALL be of a port type.

examples.text: myPort.start; // starts myPort

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.2 -- a) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.

requirements.original: The stop operation disables sending and disallow receiving operations to match at the port(s).
requirements.canonical: The `stop` port operation disables sending operations at the port or ports it is applied to.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.3 -- The stop operation disables sending and disallow receiving operations to match at the port(s).

requirements.original: The stop operation disables sending and disallow receiving operations to match at the port(s).
requirements.canonical: The `stop` port operation disallows receiving operations to match at the port or ports it is applied to.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.3 -- The stop operation disables sending and disallow receiving operations to match at the port(s).

requirements.original: ( ObjectReference | ( all port ) ) "." stop
requirements.canonical: The stop port operation has the syntax ( ObjectReference | all port ) "." stop.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.3 -- ( ObjectReference | ( all port ) ) "." stop

requirements.original: If a port is defined as allowing receiving operations such as receive and getcall, the stop operation causes listening at the named port to cease.
requirements.canonical: If a port allows receiving operations, the `stop` operation causes listening at the named port to cease.
requirements.condition: the port is defined as allowing receiving operations
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.3 -- If a port is defined as allowing receiving operations such as receive and getcall, the stop operation causes listening at the named port to cease.

requirements.original: If the port is defined to allow sending operations then stop port disallows the operations such as send, call, raise, etc. to be performed.
requirements.canonical: If a port allows sending operations, sending operations such as `send`, `call` and `raise` SHALL NOT be performed at that port after a `stop` operation.
requirements.condition: the port is defined to allow sending operations and has been stopped
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.3 -- If the port is defined to allow sending operations then stop port disallows the operations such as send, call, raise, etc. to be performed.

requirements.original: To cease listening at the port means that all receiving operations defined before the stop operation shall be completely performed before the working of the port is suspended.
requirements.canonical: When a port is stopped, all receiving operations at that port performed before the `stop` operation SHALL be completely performed before the working of the port is suspended.

readings: Receiving operations already executed (successfully matched) before the `stop` operation are completed, i.e. their effects (e.g. value redirections) take place.
Receiving operations that appear textually before the `stop` operation in the behaviour are performed completely before the port is suspended.
ambiguity.issue: 'defined before the stop operation' is unclear: executed before in time or written before in the code; chose the temporal execution reading.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.3 -- To cease listening at the port means that all receiving operations defined before the stop operation shall be completely performed before the working of the port is suspended.

requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `stop` port operation SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.3 -- a) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.

requirements.original: The halt operation is comparable to the stop operation, but allows entries being already in the queue to be processed with receiving operations.
requirements.canonical: The `halt` port operation, unlike the `stop` port operation, allows entries already in the port queue to be processed with receiving operations.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.4 -- The halt operation is comparable to the stop operation, but allows entries being already in the queue to be processed with receiving operations.

requirements.original: ( ObjectReference | ( all port ) ) "." halt
requirements.canonical: The halt port operation has the syntax ( ObjectReference | all port ) "." halt.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.4 -- ( ObjectReference | ( all port ) ) "." halt

requirements.original: If a port allows receiving operations such as receive, trigger and getcall, the halt operation disallows receiving operations to succeed for messages and procedure call elements that enter the port queue after performing the halt operation at that port.
requirements.canonical: If a port allows receiving operations, a receiving operation SHALL NOT succeed for messages and procedure call elements that enter the port queue after the `halt` operation was performed at that port.
requirements.condition: the port allows receiving operations and has been halted
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.4 -- If a port allows receiving operations such as receive, trigger and getcall, the halt operation disallows receiving operations to succeed for messages and procedure call elements that enter the port queue after performing the halt operation at that port.

requirements.original: Messages and procedure call elements that were already in the queue before the halt operation can still be processed with receiving operations.
requirements.canonical: A receiving operation CAN process messages and procedure call elements that were already in the port queue before the `halt` operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.4 -- Messages and procedure call elements that were already in the queue before the halt operation can still be processed with receiving operations.

requirements.original: If the port allows sending operations then halt port immediately disallows sending operations such as send, call, raise, etc. to be performed.
requirements.canonical: If a port allows sending operations, sending operations such as `send`, `call` and `raise` SHALL NOT be performed at that port immediately after the `halt` operation.
requirements.condition: the port allows sending operations and has been halted
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.4 -- If the port allows sending operations then halt port immediately disallows sending operations such as send, call, raise, etc. to be performed.

requirements.original: Subsequent halt operations have no effect on the state of the port or its queue.
requirements.canonical: A `halt` operation on an already halted port has no effect on the state of the port or its queue.
requirements.condition: the port has already been halted
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.4 -- Subsequent halt operations have no effect on the state of the port or its queue.

requirements.original: Entries ahead of the marker can be processed normally.
requirements.canonical: Port queue entries ahead of the halt marker CAN be processed normally.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.4 -- Entries ahead of the marker can be processed normally.

requirements.original: After all entries in the queue ahead of the marker have been processed, the state of the port is equivalent to the stopped state.
requirements.canonical: After all port queue entries ahead of the halt marker have been processed, the state of a halted port IS equivalent to the stopped state.
requirements.condition: all entries ahead of the marker have been processed
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.4 -- After all entries in the queue ahead of the marker have been processed, the state of the port is equivalent to the stopped state.

requirements.original: NOTE 2: If a port stop operation is performed on a halted port before all entries in the queue ahead of the marker have been processed, further receive operations are disallowed immediately (i.e. the marker is virtually moved to the top of the queue).
requirements.canonical: If a `stop` operation is performed on a halted port before all entries ahead of the halt marker have been processed, further receiving operations SHALL NOT succeed at that port, effective immediately.
requirements.condition: a stop operation is performed on a halted port with unprocessed entries ahead of the marker

ambiguity.issue: NOTE uses 'receive operations' where the clause otherwise uses 'receiving operations' (covering receive, trigger, getcall etc.).

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.4 -- NOTE 2: If a port stop operation is performed on a halted port before all entries in the queue ahead of the marker have been processed, further receive operations are disallowed immediately (i.e. the marker is virtually moved to the top of the queue).

requirements.original: NOTE 3: A port start operation on a halted port clears all entries in the queue irrespectively if they arrived before or after performing the port halt operation.
requirements.canonical: A `start` operation on a halted port clears all entries in the port queue, irrespective of whether they arrived before or after the `halt` operation.
requirements.condition: the port is halted
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.4 -- NOTE 3: A port start operation on a halted port clears all entries in the queue irrespectively if they arrived before or after performing the port halt operation.

requirements.original: NOTE 4: A port clear operation on a halted port clears all entries in the queue irrespectively if they arrived before or after performing the port halt operation.
requirements.canonical: A `clear` operation on a halted port clears all entries in the port queue, irrespective of whether they arrived before or after the `halt` operation.
requirements.condition: the port is halted
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.4 -- NOTE 4: A port clear operation on a halted port clears all entries in the queue irrespectively if they arrived before or after performing the port halt operation.

requirements.original: It also virtually puts the marker at the top of the queue.
requirements.canonical: A `clear` operation on a halted port virtually puts the halt marker at the top of the port queue.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.4 -- It also virtually puts the marker at the top of the queue.

requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `halt` port operation SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.4 -- a) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.

requirements.original: ( ObjectReference | ( all port ) | ( any port )) "." checkstate "(" SingleExpression ")"
requirements.canonical: The checkstate port operation has the syntax ( ObjectReference | all port | any port ) "." checkstate "(" SingleExpression ")".
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.5 -- ( ObjectReference | ( all port ) | ( any port )) "." checkstate "(" SingleExpression ")"

requirements.original: If a port is in the state specified by the parameter, the checkstate operation returns the Boolean value true.
requirements.canonical: If a port is in the state specified by the parameter, the `checkstate` operation returns the boolean value `true`.
requirements.condition: the port is in the specified state
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.5 -- If a port is in the state specified by the parameter, the checkstate operation returns the Boolean value true.

requirements.original: If the port is not in the specified state, the checkstate operation returns the Boolean value false.
requirements.canonical: If a port is not in the state specified by the parameter, the `checkstate` operation returns the boolean value `false`.
requirements.condition: the port is not in the specified state
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.5 -- If the port is not in the specified state, the checkstate operation returns the Boolean value false.

requirements.original: Calling the checkstate operation with an invalid argument leads to an error.
requirements.canonical: Calling the `checkstate` operation with an invalid argument causes an error.
requirements.condition: the argument is invalid

readings: A `checkstate` call with an argument value not in the allowed list causes a runtime error (the argument may be computed dynamically).
A `checkstate` call with an invalid argument is rejected at compile time when the value is statically known.
ambiguity.issue: The kind of error (compile-time or runtime) is not stated; chose the general reading that an error results, either at compile time for constant arguments or at runtime otherwise.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.5 -- Calling the checkstate operation with an invalid argument leads to an error.

requirements.original: It allows to check if a port is Started, Halted or Stopped, but also if a port is Connected, Mapped or Linked (i.e. Connected or Mapped).
requirements.canonical: The `checkstate` operation CAN check whether a port is Started, Halted or Stopped.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.5 -- It allows to check if a port is Started, Halted or Stopped, but also if a port is Connected, Mapped or Linked (i.e. Connected or Mapped).

requirements.original: It allows to check if a port is Started, Halted or Stopped, but also if a port is Connected, Mapped or Linked (i.e. Connected or Mapped).
requirements.canonical: The `checkstate` operation CAN check whether a port is Connected, Mapped or Linked, where Linked means Connected or Mapped.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.5 -- It allows to check if a port is Started, Halted or Stopped, but also if a port is Connected, Mapped or Linked (i.e. Connected or Mapped).

requirements.original: The states Connected, Mapped and Linked are related to the application of the connection operations connect, disconnect, map and unmap as defined in clause 21.1.
requirements.canonical: The port states Connected, Mapped and Linked are determined by the connection operations `connect`, `disconnect`, `map` and `unmap`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.5 -- The states Connected, Mapped and Linked are related to the application of the connection operations connect, disconnect, map and unmap as defined in clause 21.1.

requirements.original: The checkstate port operation can be used with all port and any port.
requirements.canonical: The `checkstate` port operation MAY be used with `all port` and with `any port`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.5 -- The checkstate port operation can be used with all port and any port.

requirements.original: Using the checkstate operation with any port allows to test if at least one port of a test component is in the specified state.
requirements.canonical: The `checkstate` operation used with `any port` returns `true` if at least one port of the test component is in the specified state.
requirements.condition: `any port` is used
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.5 -- Using the checkstate operation with any port allows to test if at least one port of a test component is in the specified state.

requirements.original: Using the checkstate operation with all port allows to check if all ports of a component are in the specified state.
requirements.canonical: The `checkstate` operation used with `all port` returns `true` if all ports of the test component are in the specified state.
requirements.condition: `all port` is used
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.5 -- Using the checkstate operation with all port allows to check if all ports of a component are in the specified state.

requirements.original: a) The parameter of the checkstate operation shall be of type charstring and shall have one of the following values:
requirements.canonical: The parameter of the `checkstate` operation SHALL be of type `charstring`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.5 -- a) The parameter of the checkstate operation shall be of type charstring and shall have one of the following values:

requirements.original: a) The parameter of the checkstate operation shall be of type charstring and shall have one of the following values: 1) "Started" 2) "Halted" 3) "Stopped" 4) "Connected" 5) "Mapped" 6) "Linked"
requirements.canonical: The parameter of the `checkstate` operation SHALL have one of the values "Started", "Halted", "Stopped", "Connected", "Mapped" or "Linked".
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.5 -- a) The parameter of the checkstate operation shall be of type charstring and shall have one of the following values: 1) "Started" 2) "Halted" 3) "Stopped" 4) "Connected" 5) "Mapped" 6) "Linked"

requirements.original: 1) "Started"
requirements.canonical: The parameter of the `checkstate` operation MAY have the value "Started".
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.5 -- 1) "Started"

requirements.original: 2) "Halted"
requirements.canonical: The parameter of the `checkstate` operation MAY have the value "Halted".
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.5 -- 2) "Halted"

requirements.original: 3) "Stopped"
requirements.canonical: The parameter of the `checkstate` operation MAY have the value "Stopped".
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.5 -- 3) "Stopped"

requirements.original: 4) "Connected"
requirements.canonical: The parameter of the `checkstate` operation MAY have the value "Connected".
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.5 -- 4) "Connected"

requirements.original: 5) "Mapped"
requirements.canonical: The parameter of the `checkstate` operation MAY have the value "Mapped".
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.5 -- 5) "Mapped"

requirements.original: 6) "Linked"
requirements.canonical: The parameter of the `checkstate` operation MAY have the value "Linked".
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.5 -- 6) "Linked"

requirements.original: b) Calling the checkstate operation with a charstring parameter not listed in a) shall lead to an error.
requirements.canonical: Calling the `checkstate` operation with a `charstring` parameter value other than "Started", "Halted", "Stopped", "Connected", "Mapped" or "Linked" SHALL cause an error.
requirements.condition: the parameter value is not in the allowed list
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.5 -- b) Calling the checkstate operation with a charstring parameter not listed in a) shall lead to an error.

requirements.original: c) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `checkstate` port operation SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 22.5.5 -- c) The ObjectReference shall be of a port type.
